long_biography.plain_text:
A 1974 leveraged buyout of McAllister Brothers Towing & Transportation shifted William “Bill” Kallop from acquisitions work into company ownership. As part-owner and chief executive, he spent more than two decades in marine transportation before a corporate split ended the partnership. He then formed Offshore International Group, concentrating on oil and gas exploration and production in the United States and Peru.

The Peruvian operation grew across 80 offshore platforms and more than 20 million coastal acres. Kallop sold his companies in 2009 and largely retired, but he soon opened a different chapter with his son Brent. They bought and restored Hacienda La Caravedo, built a modern distillery beside its historic works and launched Pisco Portón with master distiller Johnny Schuler.

uncertainties.detail: The saved owner record gives 4 March 2019, but the exact-identity Princeton memorial and funeral-home obituary independently give 24 March 2019. A correction to 24 is proposed; birth date, death month and death year are otherwise consistent.

An official Dominican decree granted Kallop privileged naturalisation in 2012. The saved secondary-nationality control does not offer Dominican as a visible option, so the fact is retained as research evidence and no invalid select value is proposed.
The reliable record establishes a United States birth and exact date but not a city or state. The blank place-of-birth field remains unresolved.

Kallop sold his core offshore companies and largely retired in 2009. His later distilling venture is well documented, but the available record does not establish it as the principal source of remaining private wealth, so Energy is disclosed as an origin-sector fallback rather than a current-holdings claim.

The core fortune is demonstrably founder-built and acquired through Kallop's own leveraged transaction and operating career, supporting broad Self-made. His education and early professional access are documented, but the material family capital or business support needed for self_made_advantaged is not; an independent start is likewise not established.

No LinkedIn, Instagram, personal website or other personal social profile met the identity-verification threshold. As Kallop died in 2019, current name-only accounts were not treated as personal profiles.

Oil & gas exploration and production is the minimum useful active tag and captures Kallop's defining wealth-producing work. The broader Oil & gas tag would be redundant, while Spirits & distilling is an important later venture but does not outweigh the principal upstream identity within the same industry dimension.
Public disputes, allegations, private estate litigation, transient investments, vessel finance and family details unrelated to business formation were excluded as unnecessary to the durable profile.
